content: The content provided appears to be a detailed and technical compilation of references, study characteristics, and evidence summaries related to the management of chronic low back pain, including pharmacological, non-pharmacological, and herbal interventions. 1. A 2023 study published in the Journal of Orthopaedic and Sports Physical Therapy emphasized the importance of systems and support in ensuring equitable musculoskeletal healthcare. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed frameworks for integrated, people-centered health services, as well as meaningful engagement of individuals living with non-communicable diseases, mental health conditions, and neurological disorders. 3. A 2014 international survey by Swain et al., published in BMC Public Health, investigated the prevalence and characteristics of pain in adolescents, highlighting the global burden of this issue. 4. Hestbaek et al. conducted an eight-year follow-up study on 9,600 twins, examining the progression of low back pain from adolescence to adulthood, as published in Spine in 2006. 5. A 2023 systematic evidence and gap map by Lyng et al., published in Pain, reviewed the current knowledge and gaps in understanding chronic musculoskeletal pain. 6. Suman et al. conducted a systematic review in 2021, published in Disability and Rehabilitation, evaluating the effectiveness of mass media campaigns in managing low back pain. 7. O’Sullivan et al. outlined ten essential facts about back pain in a 2020 article in the British Journal of Sports Medicine, aiming to dispel common misconceptions and promote evidence-based management. 8. Hayden et al. performed a network meta-analysis in 2021, published in Journal of Physiotherapy, to determine which types of exercise are most effective for individuals with chronic low back pain. 9. The WHO released guidelines for the non-surgical management of chronic primary low back pain in adults, focusing on primary and community care settings. 10. Chou et al. conducted a systematic scoping review in 2018, published in Health Expectations, to explore patients’ perceived needs for allied health and complementary medicine in managing low back pain. 11. Chiarotto et al. 12. Dworkin et al. 13. Ashton-James et al. highlighted the significance of social outcomes in pain management research and practice in a 2022 article in Pain. 14. Hickey et al. 15. Gorrell et al. updated a systematic review in 2023, published in BMJ Open, on the reporting of adverse events associated with spinal manipulation in randomized clinical trials. 16. The GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations) framework was used to assess evidence certainty in trials, considering factors such as risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision, and publication bias. 17. Trials evaluating systemic pharmacotherapy agents for chronic low back pain included opioids, NSAIDs, antidepressants, and anticonvulsants. These trials varied in sample size, participant demographics, and treatment duration, with most conducted in high-income countries. 18. Herbal medicine trials for chronic low back pain evaluated agents such as cayenne pepper, devil’s claw, and white willow bark. These studies assessed various formulations, including topical and oral preparations, with treatment durations ranging from weeks to months. 19. The WHO guidelines also reviewed the effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions, such as education, advice, massage, cognitive behavioral therapy, and physical supports like lumbar braces. 20. The evidence for many interventions, including glucocorticoids, anticonvulsants, and certain herbal medicines, remains uncertain or of low certainty, with varying impacts on benefits, harms, and resource considerations. 21. The acceptability, feasibility, and equity of interventions were also evaluated, with some treatments showing moderate costs and uncertain impacts on equity and human rights. This summary reflects the detailed findings and judgments from the referenced studies and guidelines, emphasizing the complexity and variability in managing chronic low back pain.
